key_points: DeepSeek API is OpenAI-format compatible, so OpenAI SDK + OpenAI-compatible instrumentors work for DeepSeek

No-code auto-instrumentation recommended: pip install opentelemetry-distro, opentelemetry-exporter-otlp, opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx, opentelemetry-instrumentation-system-metrics, openai, openinference-instrumentation-openai
Run opentelemetry-bootstrap --action=install, set root logger to INFO for log capture
Client uses base_url=https://api.deepseek.com with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, model deepseek-chat
Correlate traces, logs, metrics in unified dashboards; alert on latency and error rates
OpenLIT auto-instruments DeepSeek models (via OpenAI SDK) with OpenTelemetry, adding cost tracking and token usage monitoring
Compatible with OpenAI Python SDK client >= 1.13.0
One-line init: openlit.init(otlp_endpoint=...) or zero-code via openlit-instrument CLI / OTEL_* env vars
Tracks performance, token usage, costs, and user interaction without manual per-LLM setup
Instrument DeepSeek apps with OpenTelemetry and export LLM telemetry via OTLP into Cribl Search
High-level steps: configure an OTel Source in Cribl Search to receive OTLP, instrument the DeepSeek app (Node.js or Python), explore LLM telemetry use cases
Supports masking sensitive prompts/completions, emitting cost/usage metrics from token counts, sampling/throttling high-volume telemetry

Provides opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai package for OpenAI-compatible APIs (covers DeepSeek)
Backed by Y Combinator; active release/commit cadence
The 'harness' context: lm-evaluation-harness is the standard LLM evaluation framework
CLI refactored (2025/12) with subcommands run/ls/validate and YAML config via --config
Lighter install: base package no longer bundles transformers/torch; install backends separately (lm_eval[hf], lm_eval[vllm])
Supports stripping CoT reasoning traces via think_end_token arg

stats.fact: DeepSeek's API is OpenAI-format compatible, so OpenAI SDK and OpenAI-compatible OpenTelemetry instrumentors can be reused for DeepSeek tracing.
OpenLIT auto-instruments DeepSeek via the OpenAI SDK, requiring OpenAI Python SDK client >= 1.13.0.

OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions moved to a dedicated repo (open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai) and are in Development status; key attributes include gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, gen_ai.provider.name, gen_ai.token.type.
The GenAI inference span SHOULD be CLIENT kind with span name '{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}'.
lm-evaluation-harness (the standard LLM eval harness) refactored its CLI in Dec 2025 to subcommands (run/ls/validate) with YAML config support.
OpenLLMetry (traceloop) is Apache-2.0 licensed and YC-backed, providing opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai for OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs.

angles: DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible API means you can reuse the entire OpenAI OpenTelemetry instrumentation ecosystem — no custom DeepSeek SDK needed

Zero-code vs one-line vs manual instrumentation trade-offs for a harness (opentelemetry-bootstrap, openlit-instrument, or explicit SDK)
Use the official GenAI semantic conventions (gen_ai.* attributes) for standardized, queryable traces across providers
Correlate traces with token usage and cost metrics to catch regressions in DeepSeek eval runs
Streaming vs non-streaming spans, and capturing time-to-first-token for latency-sensitive harness runs
